# generator-shortcuts

The strongest plausible canonical-fitting shortcut is **“equal area implies both features match”**: whenever two panels have equal area, emit relation code `6` without checking holes. Equivalently, the learner can believe code `2` never occurs. Both versions fit all five usable canonical pairs because none contains equal-area panels with different hole counts.

An exact disagreeing input is:

```text
0 2 2 0 7 7 7
2 2 2 0 7 0 7
2 2 2 0 7 7 7
```

The left panel is a connected area-8 solid with 0 holes; the right panel is an area-8 ring with 1 hole. The intended output is:

```text
5 2
2 5
```

The shortcut instead returns:

```text
5 6
6 5
```

I checked the intended output through the supported canonical Racket path:

```sh
python3 run_with_racket.py python3 -m arcpuzzles apply fa5bb24054bc \
  --input ../checks/shortcut-witness/input.json \
  --out ../checks/shortcut-witness/racket.json
```

The report executed rule hash `b6e6c6e2c73c` and returned `[[5,2],[2,5]]`; the compact comparison is in `checks/shortcut-witness/witness.json`.

The repaired generator emits this semantic case deliberately. `sample_index % 4 == 0` selects an area-only profile, and every four consecutive samples contain at least one area-only witness. In the final production census, both canonical-fitting shortcuts were refuted in every one of 300 lessons; the independent 300-sample qualifier refuted each shortcut 213 times.
